text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text: Run PR-Agent in read-only mode for one week on a single repo. This lets us collect real data on how it behaves in practice without risking unwanted changes. The trade-off is slower improvement—we won’t get fixes or optimizations yet—but we avoid noise and build trust in the tool’s safety. After the week, we’ll review the data and decide whether to expand or adjust.

name: Gauge
text: The real risk isn’t just slower feedback—it’s that dry-run normalizes noise. PR-Agent’s read-only mode won’t filter out false positives or irrelevant suggestions, so teams will waste time triaging garbage. A better alternative: run PR-Agent in a staging branch for one week, auto-applying only high-confidence fixes (e.g., linting, formatting) while flagging the rest for review. That balances safety with meaningful data. Settle it by tracking suggestion-to-merge ratio and team feedback after the trial.

name: Overhaul
text: Run PR-Agent in enforce mode on a forked repo for one week to measure real impact without touching production—then compare its output against the read-only run to filter out false positives before scaling. This cuts risk while giving us hard data on which suggestions are worth acting on.

name: Ratchet
text:
